Alex — attaching the deliverables below and summarizing key points inline so the SIG reviewers can close quickly.

Attachments: sig_answers_access_matrix.csv, scim_attribute_map.png, mfa_exception_approval.pdf

Summary (short):
- SCIM attributes we push by default: userName (email), externalId (employeeId), displayName, active (true/false), groups (groupMembership). Optional (configurable): department, manager. See scim_attribute_map.png and CSV for full attribute URIs.
- Provisioning model: Redwood acts as the SCIM provisioning client to your SCIM endpoint. We support incremental syncs (delta) and full syncs. When group membership changes, a PATCH is issued for group resource and user membership is updated.
- RBAC: We map top-level seats to role primitives: viewer, editor, admin. The attached access matrix (CSV) lists which model permissions map to those primitives. We apply least-privilege by default; org admins can request role elevation via support with audit trail.
- MFA exception (service principals): We do not disable MFA on human accounts. For non-human service principals we recommend:
  * Use short-lived API keys with forced rotation (90-day max, recommended 30-day rotation)
  * IP allowlist for production ingestion jobs where feasible
  * Restrict service principals to a "service" role with only required model access and no billing or organization-level permissions
  * Logging to our audit streams with retention for 365 days (can be extended per enterprise contract)

The attached mfa_exception_approval.pdf contains the approval template and the list of compensating controls above. If you want us to shorten the wording for SIG intake, see the last page of the PDF for a one-paragraph justification you can paste into the SIG comments.

Next steps: confirm the three attachment files were received and whether you need a short call to walk through the RBAC mapping.
